Definition: from G165; perpetual (also used of past time, or past and future as well):--eternal, for ever, everlasting, world (began).
BiblicalUsage: The young ruler asks what good thing he must do to have eternal life; Jesus tells Nicodemus God so loved the world that whoever believes should not perish, but have everlasting life; Paul sets the wages of sin is death against the gift of God is eternal life; and Timothy hears that God's purpose and grace were given before the world began. The word always points past time, in both directions.
TheologicalSignificance: Eternal life is not life that goes on and on — it is life of a different kind, God's own life, given as a gift and not earned. I believe that is the whole gospel in one adjective: what sin pays is death, and what God gives is forever.
